dell_baseline_drift.badge: 🟡 BIOS Drift: 2 Warnings (66.7% Compliant)

drifts.rationale: System Profile is set to Dell Active Power Controller (DAPC) (PerfPerWattOptimizedDapc). Subsystem dynamic throttling can introduce slight tail latency variations under intense vSAN ESA storage I/O bursts. For peak deterministic throughput, VMware recommends configuring OS Controlled Mode or Performance Optimized (which tunes power and ASPM by proxy).
drifts.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Power Management BIOS Settings (p. 21)

drifts.rationale: PCIe ASPM is Enabled (Enabled). In storage-dense nodes loaded with NVMe SSDs or high-speed 25GbE/100GbE NICs, PCIe ASPM dynamically drops PCIe bus links into low-power states (L0s/L1) during brief I/O lulls. The exit wake latency can trigger ESXi vsandevicemonitord abort timeouts (>2,000,000 µs), risking NVMe controller resets or packet drops under bursty vSAN storage syncs. Recommended: Disabled (L0sL1Off), or apply Performance Optimized profile.
drifts.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Network Hardware Considerations (p. 19)

drifts.rationale: SR-IOV Global Enable is Disabled (Disabled). PCIe adapters cannot allocate Virtual Functions for direct-path I/O or DPU/SmartNIC offloads. Informational: Enable if Virtual Functions or DPU passthrough are required.
drifts.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Network Hardware Considerations (p. 19)

drifts.rationale: CPU Power Management is set to energy saving mode (SysDbpm). Recommended: MaxPerf or OsDbpm.
drifts.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Power Management BIOS Settings (p. 21)

rules.rationale: System Profile is set to Dell Active Power Controller (DAPC) (PerfPerWattOptimizedDapc). rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Power Management BIOS Settings (p. 21)

rules.rationale: Sub-NUMA Clustering (SNC) is Disabled (Disabled) — recommended default for general-purpose virtualization and mixed VM sizes. rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Snoop Mode Selection (p. 28)

rules.rationale: Intel VMD is Disabled. NVMe SSDs operate in native PCIe pass-through mode for direct ESXi kernel and vSAN ESA attachment.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, NVMe Storage (p. 17)

rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Network Hardware Considerations (p. 19)

rules.rationale: Logical Processor (Hyper-Threading / SMT) is Enabled. All hardware execution threads are available to ESXi schedulers.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, General BIOS Settings (p. 21)

rules.rationale: System Boot Mode is UEFI. Fully compliant with VCF 9.1, UEFI Secure Boot, TPM 2.0 attestation, and NVMe boot devices.

rules.rationale: Processor C-States are Enabled (Enabled). VMware recommends activating all C-states in BIOS to allow ESXi Host Power Management full flexibility and maximize Turbo Boost frequency headroom on active cores when idle cores enter deep sleep states.
rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, Power Management BIOS Settings (p. 21–22)

rules.citation: vSphere 9.0 Performance Best Practices, General BIOS Settings (p. 21)
